messages:
samir: Heads-up — hitting intermittent truncation on chunked streaming responses after an automatic retry on slow cellular (3G). Repro in sdk/android-sample/streaming. App thinks stream finished mid payload. Repro ~60% on network throttle. Logs below.

samir: log snippet:
```
W/OkHttp: attempt to re-open connection for canceled stream
E/StreamReader: java.io.EOFException: null
    at okio.RealBufferedSource.readUtf8LineStrict(RealBufferedSource.kt:220)
    at com.redwood.sdk.StreamingClient$readLoop(StreamingClient.kt:87)
```

anya: which OkHttp/Retrofit versions? is this our default client?

samir: okhttp 4.10.0, retrofit 2.9. Our SDK client uses retryOnConnectionFailure(true) and default ConnectionPool. Endpoint is chunked Transfer-Encoding, we consume via ResponseBody.source() without full buffering.

chandra: interesting — OkHttp will attempt to recover on some connection failures but if the response body was partially read there is nothing to reassemble, so you can observe partial payloads if a retry happens. For true streaming endpoints we usually recommend disabling retryOnConnectionFailure and tuning timeouts/connection reuse.

samir: set retryOnConnectionFailure(false) and reran: truncation rate dropped but now more early failures (no retries). Stack shows EOFException expecting N more bytes.

anya: how are you reading the stream exactly? code snippet?

samir: ```kotlin
val src = response.body!!.source()
while (!src.exhausted()) {
  val chunk = src.readUtf8Line()
  onChunk(chunk)
}
```

chandra: readUtf8Line() can be brittle for binary-ish chunk boundaries and may block; try reading into a buffer with read(sink, bufferSize) and treat -1 as EOF. Also for long lived streaming set readTimeout to 0 (no timeout) rather than large finite value. For debugging you can also set ConnectionPool(0,1,TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS) to disable reuse.

leo: also double-check interceptors: network interceptors that compress/decompress or buffer can cause different windowing. We added an opt-in builder for streaming endpoints in our internal client: enableStreaming() that does: retryOnConnectionFailure(false), readTimeout(0), and small connectionPool for single-use connections. That pattern reduced truncation in our tests.

samir: trying that now — preliminary: readTimeout(0) + retryOff reduced truncation and keeps connection open longer. But need to ensure we don't leak sockets.

ci-bot: reproduced on CI with emulator network throttle. Marked as flaky test: #infra/flake-streaming. Attached emulator commands used.

samir: created PR with opt-in builder + sample docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/java-sdk/pull/764 — includes sample app update and a small integration that mocks socket close mid-stream.

anya: QA note: update sample app README with emulator network throttle instructions and adb commands for delay and bandwidth limits. Also add a note to dev onboarding about streaming flag.

samir: added docs and sample commands to PR, included `adb shell svc data disable/enable` and `adb shell network delay` snippets.

chandra: thanks — LGTM once CI stabilizes. :thumbsup:

samir: thanks all — will follow up if we see regressions.
